Title: Partial Card Usage: A Possible Explination

Messages.Author: Jerry Jackson
Messages.Body:
I have been reading several posts about Anarch Troublemaker, Domain,
Acrobatics, and the usage of part of these cards. If you notice, Anarch
Troublemake can have a partial effect, tap 1 or 2 vamps, while Domain and
Acrobatics require the entire condition to be satisfied. I think I have a
possible explination:

Anarch Troublemaker is a Master Card, which represents the influence and
power of the Methesula. The other two are normal cards, played by vampires who
are puppets of the Methusela. Looking at it this way, a Methusela's power
versusa vampire's power. The Methusela can dictate term (the Blood Rule - He
who has the blood makes the rules) whereas a vampire, who was influence by the
Methusela, is bound by his physical limitations (normal vs superior) and
the only influence he has is which skills he has and how much of his skill he
wants to use (normal or superior where applicable), but can't dictate terms
once determined (must use card in it's entirty, i.e. superior Acrobatics:
Dodge AND Additional Strike). This privelege is reserved for Methusela.

That's one possibility.

Messages.Author: Jeremy York
Messages.Body:
The way I see it is as follows (no nice rationalizations about
the game world, though, sorry, just boring rules/logic gunk):

Say a card does A and B.

If, for some reason, using the card would cause A but not B,
this is fine.

If, however, B happens to be illegal at a particular time,
then the card can't be used.

That is, just because one of the effects of the card will be
nullified or without a target doesn't stop you from playing
the cardn (Anarch Troublemaker). If one of the effects isn't
allowed, that's a different story (the intercept on
Tradition : Domain to block a steath-less action).
--
Jeremy (bea...@netcom.com, bea...@delphi.com)

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
The rulebook says "Only one card may give an additional strike to a minion for
each round of combat", not "A minion can only play one additional strike
card each round". Since you can play any card even if you expect not to get
some or all of the effect, you can therefore keep burning additional strike
cards once you've used one in a round. If you want to argue that one
*shouldn't* be able to burn additional strike cards, that's fine, but to
actually rule that way would directly contradict the rulebook, and the
general rule about playing effects.


>

This logic is counter to the logic you use to deny the playing of second
tradition unless Prince is both tapped and in need of intercept.

Superior Acrobatics: Strike: Dodge with an Additional Strike.
2nd Tradition: Untap with +2 intercept. (Or, literal reading: +2 intercept
with optional untap).

You say: can use Strike dodge without invoking additional strike.
but
You say: cannot use untap without invoking (needing) intercept.
and
You say: cannot use intercept without invoking (needing) untap.

The rules state "Only one card may give an additional strike to a minion for
each round of combat", but they also state: "Players cannot increase ...
intercept beyond that needed to counter directly another player's increase
of stealth..."

-----
Burning cards with no effects is fine, but should be a general case
for all cards - without making unfounded exceptions for 2nd Tradition.
Burning cards for partial effect is certainly more easy to swallow than
burning cards for no effect.
-----

What's the reason for this inconsistency?

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
If a card says it is only usable by a certain type of minion, then it
really is only usable by that type of minion. For example, a card that
says "Only usable by a Justicar" can only be played by a Justicar;
non-Justicars cannot play it just to burn it. However, if it is legal
for a minion to play a card in the first place, it can play that card
even if it will result in no or partial effect.

Additionally, there are a few rules that place blanket restrictions on
using effects, and are exceptions to the "laissez faire" rule of thumb.
For example, you simply cannot increase a minion's stealth unless it is
trying to overcome another minion's intercept. For better or worse, the
description of additional strikes in the Jyhad rulebook does not prohibit
you from playing more than one addstrike card during a round. It just says
that the minion won't get any effect from the later ones.

Domain has several potential restrictions on its use. First, it's only
usable by a prince or justicar (first line), so primogen, kine, and
untitled kindred cannot even think about playing it. Second, it gives +2
intercept, so it may not be used unless the vampire is attempting to
override another vampire's stealth. Third, it says that it's (only) usable
by a tapped vampire, so an untapped prince or justicar may attempt to play it.
If the card had been written "This vampire untaps and attempts to block",
then this last restriction would not have applied.


